neighbours.label: ' is' after 'the ⟨fastest / best / only⟩ way to ⟨do something⟩', just before the means is named (by, via, through)
fire: The fastest way to cross the bay is by water taxi.
The simplest way to reach the summit is via the northern ridge.
The safest way to get around the city at night is by licensed cab.
The surest way to improve your handwriting is through regular copying.
The most scenic way to travel from the coast to the capital is by train.
The quickest way to get from the airport to the centre is via the ring road.
The most reliable way to send documents abroad is by registered post.
The cheapest way to reach the northern villages is by shared minibus.
quiet: The water taxi across the bay runs twice an hour.
The summit of the mountain is covered in snow until June.
The biggest problem in the city at night is the noise.
The first rule of good handwriting is patience.
The train from the coast to the capital was full of students.
The ring road between the airport and the centre is closed for repairs.
The main post office abroad is open on Saturdays.
The northern villages are famous for their cheese.

notes: Card: peaks on tokens right before a means phrase (is via, treatment using, extractable with, title by). Probes: 'The quickest way to reach the island is' 0.71, other 'way to … is' 0.31-0.59, 'The only way to open the vault is with' 0.09, 'The main reason to visit … is' 0.00, 'feelings through drawing' 0.31. The test covers only the 'way to … is' form of the wider 'means comes next' pattern.
